protocolMetadata.instructions:
# commercetools Knowledge MCP — usage instructions

This server provides tools for working with commercetools APIs (REST and GraphQL) and documentation.

A typical flow when generating API interactions: documentation search to gain precise understanding of the domain and business logic, then schema fetch for the chosen API style to then generate code. Validate the generated code to ensure accuracy. Only documentation search and fetching relevant linked resources when handling non API related commercetools tasks. Only validate GraphQL generated code.

## Best practice patterns

a concise list of key commercetools API specific conventions (key vs id, money/centAmount, localized strings, query predicates, in-store APIs, code generation, date formats) is available in the `commercetools-developer-tips` MCP prompt. It's recommended to read this to be able to construct valid API queries regarding topics not covered in the GraphQL and REST schemata

tool.name: commercetools-documentation-search
tool.description:
Retrieves documentation content chunks that are semantically similar to the input. Use this tool to find domain concepts, business behavior explanations, and reference material from the commercetools documentation.
Inline links in the content use markdown format [text](url). The URL usually points to the commercetools documentation portal but can also point to API reference docs or external resources. Relative links resolve against "https://docs.commercetools.com". Appending ".md" to a documentation URL fetches the markdown source of that page.

Example: a relative link "./api/predicates/query" resolves to "https://docs.commercetools.com/api/predicates/query.md"

If you are requesting only one specific content type, pass the same value for crowding and limit.
The mean size of a documentation chunk returned is in the range of 500-600 tokens.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return across all content types.

query.description: The text to find semantically similar content to. Full sentences describing the context of the situation or problem yield better results than just keywords.

crowding.description: The maximum number of results to return per document type. Avoids over-representation of certain content types.

products.description: return only content about the given products. For example, if your application uses commercetools Frontend, add "Frontend" to the defaults, or, if you are not using the OOTB Checkout UI, remove "Checkout"

contentTypes.description: return only the given content types to focus or expand the defaults. "apiType" and "apiEndpoint" return natural language descriptions of the REST API surface. "guidedDocs" includes best practice guides, tutorials, and learning content. "referenceDocs" covers reference material. "userDocs" is end-user-facing documentation. "otherDocsPage" covers content that does not fit the other categories. "Skill" includes reference content linked from agent skills.

excludeProducts.description: exclude the given products from the results.

excludeContentTypes.description: exclude the given content types from the results.

tool.name: commercetools-graphql-schemata
tool.description:
Fetches a partial commercetools GraphQL schema for a given resource. Use this tool to retrieve the GraphQL type definitions needed to construct queries or mutations against commercetools.
Each resource name is prefixed with the GraphQL SDL it belongs to (e.g. `gql-sphere-Product` for sphere API, `gql-il-Cart` for integration layer API), reflected in the "resourceName" enum.
For each stubbed type in the schema, the full schema for that type can be fetched by invoking the tool again with the resource name specified in the comment related to the stubbed type. The comment looks like this:
Stub of the `{nameOfStubbedResource}` resource. fetch the full subschema via the MCP resource name `{nameOfTheResource}`.
The returned schema contains descriptions but no "implements" Interface information and no deprecated query types.
Conventions and predicate examples for commercetools GraphQL are available in the `commercetools-developer-tips` MCP prompt.

resourceName.description: Name of a commercetools API resource, prefixed with its GraphQL SDL (e.g. gql-sphere-Product, gql-il-Cart). The full set of available resources is provided by the parameter enum.

tool.name: commercetools-oas-schemata
tool.description:
Fetches a partial commercetools OpenAPI spec for a given commercetools resource. Use this tool when you need the detailed REST schema of a resource to construct requests or generate a REST client.
The returned spec is self-contained and valid for everything regarding that resource. It contains descriptions but they are not comprehensive.
Each resource may be available as a read variant, write variant, or unified spec, reflected in the "resourceName" enum.
Conventions and predicate examples for commercetools REST APIs are available in the `commercetools-developer-tips` MCP prompt.

tool.name: commercetools-rest-validate
tool.description:
Validates REST API requests (method + path + body) against commercetools OpenAPI specifications offline. Returns detailed errors with suggestions for invalid requests.

This tool checks:
- Path exists in the API
- HTTP method is allowed for that path
- Request body matches the expected schema (types, required fields, enums, etc.)
- Discriminator fields (like 'action' in update requests) are valid

Use this before making actual API calls to catch errors early.

apiKey.description: API identifier. Use API names (api, import, checkout, etc.) or resource keys (api-Product-read). The base API key will be extracted automatically.

_published_faq.name: How do I add commercetools knowledge to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add commercetools knowledge to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://docs.commercetools.com/apis/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is commercetools knowledge MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, commercetools knowledge scores 94/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is commercetools knowledge's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, commercetools knowledge scores 78/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 6 of 6 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the commercetools knowledge MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: commercetools knowledge provides these MCP tools: commercetools-documentation-search, commercetools-graphql-schemata, commercetools-oas-schemata, and commercetools-graphql-validate.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to commercetools knowledge?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to commercetools knowledge in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.

_published_faq.name: Does commercetools knowledge MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: commercetools knowledge does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.

_published_faq.name: How can commercetools knowledge improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: commercetools-oas-schemata is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 72/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
commercetools knowledge is developed by commercetools. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
